question: Is the R4 fresh-pair maintenance negative attributable to paired-delta target-ranking failure, insufficient unchanged validation sensitivity for exact-target repair, or both?
hypothesis: Across eight independently reconstructed rows on the exact R4 fresh pair, at least one true damaged target will not rank first under the frozen paired-delta monitor and at least one exact-target canonical restoration will fail the unchanged 0.20 selected-key validation-gain and 0.005 BPB retain rule, classifying the fresh-pair boundary as mixed monitor-and-validation failure rather than sequential carryover alone.
authority: diagnostic research-only; no learner, corpus, monitor, threshold, target schedule, degradation, repair, validation, capacity, deployment, external-model inference, scheduler, queue, broker, accepted-ref, runtime, or authority changes

arms_and_inputs.design: one diagnostic matrix of eight independent rows plus a byte-identical replay of the prior sequential R4 aggregate as a provenance/cardinality control
arms_and_inputs.training: exact WLM-LM-REAL-UTF8-BYTE-PILOT-R2 four training Git blobs and byte-identical TrainModel path
arms_and_inputs.segmentation: Each evaluation blob is split by raw byte index into the unchanged four contiguous quarters with context reset at boundaries.
arms_and_inputs.target_schedule: byte-identical R4 eligibility, distinct-target rule, ordering, and four scheduled targets per file
arms_and_inputs.monitor_diagnostic: For each row independently degraded from canonical state, rank the frozen stored-healthy paired degraded-minus-healthy scores without target or class access and record true-target rank, top1 identity, score, and margin.
arms_and_inputs.repair_diagnostic: On a separate clone of the same independently degraded row, restore the evaluator-known true target's exact canonical record, apply the unchanged validation retain rule, and measure audit restoration. Target identity is evaluator-only and never enters monitor ranking.
arms_and_inputs.sequential_control: Invoke the byte-identical frozen R4 implementation and require its complete normalized aggregate to reproduce the prior negative's exact cardinalities and scalar metrics.

seeds.determinism: Git blob identities, raw-byte quarter boundaries, frozen class order, occurrence/gain ordering, and lexicographic raw-key tie breaks determine every row

controls: Reuse the exact R4 training blobs, evaluation blobs, blob hashes, quarter segmentation, class order, target schedule, degradation constructors, canonical model, stored healthy profile, paired-delta score, eligibility, and raw-key tie break.
Reuse the exact R4 0.20 selected-key validation-gain and 0.005 global-BPB retain thresholds without alteration.
Reconstruct every diagnostic row from canonical state so earlier failed or retained repairs cannot contaminate later attribution rows.
Compute monitor attribution and exact-target repair attribution on separate clones of the same independently degraded row.
Keep target and class identity unavailable to monitor ranking; evaluator-only target access is limited to rank measurement and the preregistered exact-target counterfactual.
Run the prior sequential implementation only as an unchanged replay control; its output cannot select or modify diagnostic behavior.
Use no tokenizer, randomness, external model, retraining, capacity growth, class-dependent policy, live canonical shadow, or live interface.
validity_criteria: Exact parent SHA, North Star path/hash, prior negative identity, qualification identity, and classification identity match.
Training and evaluation Git blob identities match; the two evaluation blobs remain disjoint from the pilot and R1/R2 evaluation sets.
The frozen R4 schedule yields exactly four distinct targets per file and all eight independent rows complete in the frozen class order.
Quarter boundaries, degradation constructors, canonical model, healthy profile, monitor pairing, eligibility, score, tie break, repair, validation, and audit semantics are byte-identical to R4.
The unchanged sequential replay reproduces every preregistered R4 control scalar exactly, including the four-retain/four-revert cardinality and audit maxima.
Every independent row starts from canonical state and the monitor and exact-target counterfactual operate on separate clones.
No target or class label enters monitor ranking; no tokenizer, randomness, external model, retraining, capacity growth, threshold change, or authority widening occurs.
Full Go regression passes before probe execution and the normalized result carries the exact experiment identity.

classification_rules.monitor_only: Validity passes, monitor_top1_target_count is less than 8, and exact_target_repair_retain_count is 8 with exact audit restoration in all rows.
classification_rules.validation_only: Validity passes, monitor_top1_target_count is 8, and exact_target_repair_retain_count is less than 8 or exact audit restoration fails in at least one row.
classification_rules.mixed: Validity passes, monitor_top1_target_count is less than 8, and exact_target_repair_retain_count is less than 8 or exact audit restoration fails in at least one row.
classification_rules.no_independent_failure: Validity passes, monitor_top1_target_count and exact_target_repair_retain_count are both 8 with exact audit restoration in all rows; the prior negative is then attributable to sequential interaction not reproduced by either isolated component.
classification_rules.incomplete: Compute interruption prevents the complete frozen eight-row matrix or single sequential replay without violating a validity criterion.
classification_rules.invalid: Any identity, provenance, schedule, segmentation, degradation, monitor, repair, validation, replay cardinality, deterministic construction, capacity, or qualification criterion drifts.

stop_conditions: Stop invalid before scientific execution if any parent, North Star, evidence, blob, overlap, schedule, build/regression, or frozen-control identity check fails.
